line.town.stones_kid.3: You throw it low, almost along the water.
line.town.stones_kid.5: All the good stones are in the sea already. We threw them there.
line.town.stones_grown.1: The hand remembers. Three skips, but it remembers.
line.town.stones_grown.2: Water this smooth, it'd be a sin not to.
line.town.paper_bench.1: The cable car again. Every day it's the cable car.
line.town.paper_bench.2: They promise one weather, and there's another outside.
line.town.paper_bench.3: Notices first, then the news. It's more interesting that way.
line.town.paper_bench.4: The crossword's easy today. Almost a pity.
line.town.paper_bench.5: Morning, a bench, the paper. Nothing else needed.
line.town.dominoes.2: Double six on the table. Who's brave?
line.town.dominoes.3: Don't slam them so, the cups are jumping.
line.town.dominoes.5: I believe you're counting my tiles.
line.town.cure.1: Three sips before meals. The doctor said not to hurry.
line.town.cure.2: The water's warm and salty. So it must be good for you.
line.town.cure.3: Treatments in the morning, dominoes after lunch. A regimen.
line.town.cure.4: The knee's better already. Or I just want it to be.
line.town.allotment_dig.1: The soil here is sand and more sand. Nothing without compost.
line.town.allotment_dig.2: Got to get it dug while it's cool.
line.town.allotment_dig.3: Weeds grow by themselves, carrots need persuading.
line.town.allotment_dig.4: The neighbour's bed is straighter. Never mind, I've got the dill.
line.town.allotment_water.1: You water in the evening, once the sun's gone.
line.town.allotment_water.2: At the root, at the root, not over the leaves.
line.town.allotment_water.3: Third can. Two more, and home.
line.town.allotment_hero.1: And how's your bed? Don't forget to water it.
line.town.post_round.1: Third entrance, two postcards and a magazine.
line.town.post_round.2: By noon the bag's lighter and the legs are heavier.
line.town.post_round.3: Those who get letters wait at the door.
line.town.post_round.4: Rain or wind, the post goes round.
line.town.post_round_hero.1: For you? Look in the box by the club, that's where I leave it.
line.town.cinema_house.2: I've seen this newsreel before. Still good.
line.town.cinema_house.3: My row's the seventh. Always the seventh.
line.town.piano_hall.1: Out of tune, of course. But the hall forgives.
line.town.piano_hall.2: Nobody here in the evening. You're allowed mistakes.
line.town.piano_hall.3: They set me this one back in music school.
line.town.aton_nets.1: A net's like a memory: where it tore is where something happened.
line.town.aton_nets.2: A knot, another knot. That'll take me to lunch.
line.town.aton_nets.3: Thirty years at sea, now on a bench. Same net.
line.town.aton_nets.4: Wind from the west. More drying tomorrow.
line.town.aton_nets.5: That's no hole. It's the herring's way in, with no way out.
line.town.aton_nets_hero.1: Don't touch the needle, it's the only one I've got.
line.town.aton_nets_hero.2: Sit down if you're not in a hurry. Nobody's in a hurry here.
line.town.aton_boats.1: Boats are like old men: lying belly up, watching the sea.
line.town.aton_boats.2: My father tarred this one. It still holds.
line.town.aton_boats.3: The sea's quieter in the evening. You can hear the brook going into it.
line.town.aton_hives.1: Come quietly. They're not angry, they're busy.
line.town.aton_hives.2: A bee flies to where the apple tree was in bloom. It remembers.
line.town.aton_hives.3: You don't go to them without smoke. It's like knocking.
line.town.aton_hives.4: The honey's got heather in it this year. A touch bitter.
line.town.aton_picnic.1: The apples here are nobody's. So they're everybody's.
line.town.aton_picnic.2: Pass the salt. No, the cucumbers later.
line.town.aton_picnic.3: Only half an hour's walk from town, and it's like we went away.
line.town.aton_hide.2: The same every evening, and different every evening.
line.town.aton_hide.3: The falcon's here already. See how they've closed up?
line.town.aton_hide.4: Writing it down: fog, six degrees, a thousand and more.
line.town.aton_walk.1: You can see the whole town from here.
line.town.aton_walk.2: A short climb, but the air's different.
line.town.aton_walk.3: People used to just ride the cable car up here. Walking's better.
line.town.aton_walk.4: To the birch and back. That's what we call it.
line.town.aton_walk_hero.1: Good afternoon. The lookout's not far now.
line.town.aton_walk_hero.2: Coming from Aton? Well, it's easier going down.
line.town.aton_view.1: That's our roof. Third terrace, with the aerial.
line.town.aton_view.2: The sea's grey today. So it'll clear by evening.
line.town.aton_view.3: Let's sit till the cabin goes by. I like watching it.
line.town.aton_view.4: There's always wind up here. Even when the town is still.
line.town.aton_brook.1: First across the stones is captain!
line.town.aton_brook.2: There was a fish here! This big!
line.town.aton_brook.3: Don't tell Mum I got my foot wet.
line.town.aton_brook.4: Let's dam it! It'll be a sea.
line.town.dog_owner_walk.1: Out for our walk. Twice a day, any weather. It's him who walks me.
line.town.dog_owner_walk.2: Don't be afraid, no biting. A licking, at worst.
line.town.dog_owner_walk.3: Every post has to be read. That's his newspaper.
line.town.dog_owner_walk.4: Without the dog I'd never see the promenade. As it is, every morning.
line.town.dog_owner_walk.5: On the lead, yes. There are gulls on the terraces, and we have a temper.
line.town.dog_owner_walk.6: At home he's quiet. It's outside that he has business.
line.town.dog_owner_walk.7: We walk in the rain too. Then a shake in the stairwell, and the neighbours are delighted.
line.town.dog_owner_walk_evening.1: The evening round. He knows the route better than I do.
line.town.dog_owner_walk_evening.2: At sunset he always sits and looks at the sun. I've got used to it too.
line.town.pet_talk.2: Now what have you found there? Come on, come on.
line.town.pet_talk.3: That is not food. Leave it.
line.town.pet_talk.4: The gulls have done nothing to you.
line.town.pet_talk.5: Good boy, good boy. You'll get something at home.
line.town.pet_talk.6: Don't pull. We aren't late for anything.
line.town.pet_talk.7: Said hello? Right, on we go.
line.town.pet_stroke_yes.1: You may, you may. Just let him sniff your hand first.
line.town.pet_stroke_yes.2: Go on, he loves it. He won't leave your side after.
line.town.pet_stroke_yes.3: Of course. Scratch behind the ear, that's the spot.
line.town.pet_stroke_yes.4: You may. He's the sociable one in the family.
line.town.pet_stroke_no.1: Better not. He's out of sorts today.
line.town.pet_stroke_no.2: Not now, we're in a hurry. Come up in the evening.
line.town.pet_stroke_no.3: He's shy of strangers. Come by more often, he'll get used to you.
line.town.cat_call.2: Puss-puss! There's enough for all, no shoving.
line.town.cat_call.3: Ginger, you ate for two yesterday. Fair shares today.
line.town.cat_call.4: Come on, come on. Forty years I've fed you lot, never once late.
line.town.cat_call.5: Puss-puss! And where's the grey one? On the roof again?
line.town.cat_lady_round.1: At eight and at half past six. They set their clocks by me.
line.town.cat_lady_round.2: Yard cats, but I know each one. That tabby there came as a kitten.
line.town.cat_lady_round.3: Don't fear them and don't chase them. Sit quietly, they'll come themselves.
line.town.cat_lady_round.4: I take the bowls in at night. Else the hedgehogs finish them off.
line.town.cat_sill.1: That's ours. On the sill since morning, guarding the yard.
line.town.cat_sill.2: Sits there like the landlord. And first at the door for supper.
line.town.cat_sill.3: Won't go out. Says he can see it all from there.
line.town.cat_sill.4: Don't tap on the glass, he'll take offence. He bears grudges.
line.town.hedgehog_seen.1: Quiet. The hedgehog's out. Stomps about here every evening.
line.town.hedgehog_seen.2: Don't touch, he'll curl up and sulk for half an hour.
line.town.hedgehog_seen.3: Hear him puffing? So small, and noisy as a steam engine.
line.town.hedgehog_seen.4: The cats leave him be now. One sniff was enough.
line.town.cat_friend.1: You again? Go on then, see me home.
line.town.cat_friend.2: To the door and no further. You know that yourself.
line.town.cat_friend.3: Tail straight up. So it's a good day.
line.town.cat_friend.4: I'll bring you something tomorrow. Today there was only sour cream, and that got eaten.
line.town.cat_friend.5: The whole yard feeds you, and it's me you see home. Thank you.
line.town.cat_friend.6: Well, here we are. Off you go.
line.town.cat_scrap.1: There, take it. And don't let me see you before lunch.
line.town.cat_scrap.2: A cod's tail. Don't ask for more, that's the lot.
line.town.cat_scrap.3: My best customer. Doesn't pay, but comes every day.
line.town.cat_scrap.4: Eat it here, don't drag it under the counter.
line.town.cat_scrap.5: The sprats are small today. Just right for you.
line.town.cat_shoo.2: Off you go, let me clean up.
line.town.cat_shoo.3: Not under my feet. I'll tread on you.
line.town.cat_shoo.4: Come back later. No time for you now.
line.town.cat_shoo.5: Sits there and stares, as if I were the one in his way.
line.town.guest_arrive.1: Good day. I have a voucher for two weeks.
line.town.guest_arrive.2: I walked from the train. The suitcase got heavier on the way.
line.town.guest_arrive.3: You can smell the sea right from the platform.
line.town.guest_arrive.4: A room with a sea view? Then I agree to any regime.
line.town.guest_depart.1: Two weeks like a single day.
line.town.guest_depart.2: The train's at ten forty-five. I'll stand and breathe a last while.
line.town.guest_depart.3: Amber, postcards and the local water in the suitcase. Mustn't break it.
line.town.guest_depart.4: Back here in a year. It's settled.
line.town.guest_goodbye.1: Come to see me off? Thank you. Write to me, the desk has my address.
line.town.guest_goodbye.2: Well, goodbye, my dining-room neighbour. Look after your town.
line.town.guest_goodbye.3: Good that we got to meet. I'll be back in a year to see how you've grown.
line.town.guest_promenade.1: After lunch one is meant to walk. A regime is a regime.
line.town.guest_promenade.2: To the end of the promenade and back is exactly a thousand steps. I counted.
line.town.guest_promenade.3: The doctor said: breathe the sea. I'm breathing.
line.town.guest_promenade.4: There's no air like this at home. If only I could take a jar.
line.town.guest_postcards.1: Three postcards with the lighthouse. And one with the cable car, for my grandson.
line.town.guest_postcards.2: I write home every day. They read once a week.
line.town.guest_postcards.3: "Arrived well, fed well, the water's salty." What else is there to write?
line.town.guest_gromov.1: The soup cools in eleven minutes. I timed it.
line.town.guest_gromov.2: In seventy-five they trained three of us for one ship. The first one flew.
line.town.guest_gromov.3: On the centrifuge I sang so as not to pass out. Don't ask what.
line.town.guest_gromov.4: Being ready is a flight too. I flew as far as here.
line.town.guest_mironova.1: Actually I'm here for my bronchi. The violin came along by itself.
line.town.guest_mironova.2: They only let me play until quiet hour. And the entrance exam is in September.
line.town.guest_mironova.3: There's nobody in the winter garden at five. That's where I practise.
line.town.guest_mironova.4: Yesterday people listened at the door. Two cried. They say that's not a complaint.
line.town.guest_tamm.1: Oh-seven-forty, wind north, porridge of oats. Logged.
line.town.guest_tamm.2: The rook stood on d7. Sixty-one, the club final. I remember!
line.town.guest_tamm.3: We replayed it. He won. But in sixty-one my knee didn't hurt.
line.town.guest_tamm.4: A draw is a draw. But tomorrow it'll be a north-wester, you'll see.
line.town.guest_sazonov.1: Boris and I have been friends since sixty-one. Arguing since the same year.
line.town.guest_sazonov.2: There was no rook on d7. I spent forty years teaching children not to invent the terms of a problem.
line.town.guest_sazonov.3: We rebuilt the thirty-third move on napkins. The waitress took them away.
line.town.guest_sazonov.4: I offered the draw. But don't tell him: let him wonder.
line.town.guest_krylova.1: I'm from Vologda. Thirty years at the switchboard: "Putting you through!"
line.town.guest_krylova.2: I knew the whole town by voice. Hardly anyone by face.
line.town.guest_krylova.3: One voice rang Murmansk every Friday. Twenty years. Then it stopped.
line.town.guest_krylova.4: Here on the promenade I heard it. That very voice. Asking for an ice cream.
line.town.guest_abdullina.1: I'm from Kazan, a seamstress. I see a person and know their measurements at once.
line.town.guest_abdullina.2: I sewed two hundred wedding dresses. Never had my own: we signed in the lunch break.
line.town.guest_abdullina.3: I bought some white cloth at the department store here. Don't ask what for.
line.town.guest_abdullina.4: I sew in my room in the evenings. Our golden wedding is in a year. I'll make it.
line.town.guest_levin.1: We're from Murmansk. Forty years I steered icebreakers and hardly saw a sea without ice.
line.town.guest_levin.2: The sea here is quiet. I look at it and wait for it to crack.
line.town.guest_levin.3: I get up for the dawn out of habit. The watch from four, nobody cancelled it.
line.town.guest_levin.4: Yesterday I went in up to the knees. Tamara says that already counts as a voyage.
line.town.guest_levina.1: Forty years I taught music and waited for my husband from the sea. Now he waits for me.
line.town.guest_levina.2: There's a grand piano in the hall. Out of tune, but honest.
line.town.guest_levina.3: Arkady doesn't know a single note. But he knows my footsteps from two floors away.
line.town.guest_levina.4: Tonight I'll play in the club hall. He'll sit in the last row and look at his watch. Out of pride.
line.town.guest_beketov.1: I'm from Norilsk. It's night there now, until January.
line.town.guest_beketov.2: Thirty years underground, at the mine. I saw the sun by the holiday rota.
line.town.guest_beketov.3: Here it sets into the sea every evening and nobody's surprised. I go and am surprised for everyone.
line.town.guest_beketov.4: Haruo mended my watch. He said it was running one polar night slow.
line.town.guest_matsumoto.1: I'm from Otaru. A watchmaker. We have a sea too, only from the other side.
line.town.guest_matsumoto.2: In my life I've mended nine thousand watches. One I couldn't: my father's.
line.town.guest_matsumoto.3: The dining room clock keeps exact time. I checked for three days. A rarity and a joy.
line.town.guest_matsumoto.4: I've decided not to mend my father's. Let it show his time. I have my own.
line.town.guest_kovalchuk.1: My granddaughter and I are from Irkutsk. I'm a train conductor: four days to Moscow, four back.
line.town.guest_kovalchuk.2: I didn't sleep the first night: the bed doesn't rock.
line.town.guest_kovalchuk.3: The train here crosses the sea in twenty minutes. I rode it and was upset: I'd just made the tea.
line.town.guest_kovalchuk.4: Asya asked why I carry tea round to everyone in the dining room. Habit. Nobody complains.
line.town.guest_asya.1: Granny and I were five days on the way here. I counted the bridges. A hundred and forty-two.
line.town.guest_asya.2: We have Baikal, the stones there are round. Here they're flat, just right for skipping.
line.town.guest_asya.3: My record is nine. The local kids say theirs is twelve. I won't believe it till I see it.
line.town.guest_asya.4: One stone a day I don't throw, I put it in the suitcase. Granny doesn't know yet why it's heavy.
line.town.fv_weekend_market_bring.1: I'm taking a jar of honey to the market and an empty bag. The bag comes back full.
line.town.fv_weekend_market_grump.1: Every Saturday the same: you come for dill and leave with three bags.
line.town.fv_weekend_market_kid.1: We're counting who has the biggest pumpkin on the stall. The man with the moustache is winning.
line.town.fv_weekend_market_elder.1: They used to sell straight from the boats. The fish was still jumping while they weighed it.
line.town.fv_sea_festival_bring.1: I'm bringing a flask and an old blanket to the shore. By the sea a holiday is short without one.
line.town.fv_sea_festival_grump.1: A festival of the sea, and the wind is such that you hold your hat with both hands.
line.town.fv_sea_festival_kid.1: Whoever finds the smoothest stone is captain today. I've got three already.
line.town.fv_sea_festival_elder.1: On this day our whole yard met the boats. The first to see a sail got the first bowl of soup.
line.town.fv_lantern_night_bring.1: I'm bringing spare candles. Somebody's lantern always goes out.
line.town.fv_lantern_night_grump.1: It's pretty, I won't argue. But the wax never comes out of a coat.
line.town.fv_lantern_night_kid.1: We walk in a line and don't talk. Whoever laughs carries the lantern at the back.
line.town.fv_lantern_night_elder.1: We glued the lanterns out of newspapers then. They gave little light, but they were ours.
line.town.fv_first_snow_bring.1: I'm getting out mittens for the whole family. One, as always, has no pair.
line.town.fv_first_snow_grump.1: First snow, what joy. And who clears the paths? Exactly.
line.town.fv_first_snow_kid.1: Whoever catches a snowflake on the tongue first makes a wish. Don't tell me how!
line.town.fv_first_snow_elder.1: For the first snow my mother always baked buns. The snow melts, the smell stays.
line.town.fv_winter_fair_bring.1: I'm taking knitted socks to the fair. Every year I think it's too many, and every year they run out.
line.town.fv_winter_fair_grump.1: A gingerbread costs as much as a dinner. And I'll buy it all the same.
line.town.fv_winter_fair_kid.1: We're looking for the gingerbread with the funniest icing. We found a cat with one ear.
line.town.fv_winter_fair_elder.1: At the winter fair my father and I chose felt boots. He knocked them together and listened.
line.town.fv_new_year_bring.1: I'm carrying salad in the biggest pot. This house accepts nothing smaller.
line.town.fv_new_year_grump.1: Before midnight everyone is sleepy, after midnight nobody will go to bed.
line.town.fv_new_year_kid.1: We're betting who stays awake longest. Last year I slept through the chimes.
line.town.fv_new_year_elder.1: There were tangerines once a year then. We dried the peel on the radiator till spring.
line.town.fv_maslenitsa_bring.1: I'm carrying pancakes under a towel. By the time I get there half will go to friends.
line.town.fv_maslenitsa_grump.1: Pancakes, pancakes. By the fifth day I can't look at a frying pan.
line.town.fv_maslenitsa_kid.1: We're counting who eats the most pancakes. With sour cream doesn't count, that's too easy.
line.town.fv_maslenitsa_elder.1: Our whole street made the straw doll. The straw came from the stable, the scarf from a neighbour.
line.town.fv_bird_day_bring.1: I'm carrying a nesting box. The roof went on crooked, but starlings aren't fussy.
line.town.fv_bird_day_grump.1: Bird day. And who gives me back the cherries they ate last summer?
line.town.fv_bird_day_kid.1: We're playing who knows a bird by its voice. Sparrows don't count, everybody knows them.
line.town.fv_bird_day_elder.1: Our whole class hung nesting boxes. Mine stayed on a poplar for twenty years.
line.town.fv_blossom_bring.1: I'm taking a rug and a rhubarb pie. It tastes better under an apple tree in bloom.
line.town.fv_blossom_grump.1: It blooms beautifully. And from that beauty my nose hasn't worked for three days.
line.town.fv_blossom_kid.1: Whoever gets a petal on the nose is it. No luck for me so far.
line.town.fv_blossom_elder.1: These apple trees were planted the year the cable car opened. They came up to my shoulder then.
line.town.fv_midsummer_bring.1: I'm bringing wood for the bonfire. Dry birch, kept since last year.
line.town.fv_midsummer_grump.1: The shortest night of the year, and they won't let you sleep even that.
line.town.fv_midsummer_kid.1: We're looking for the fern flower. The grown-ups say there isn't one, but they didn't look properly.
line.town.fv_midsummer_elder.1: We jumped the fire in pairs. If the hands held, there was a wedding in autumn.
line.town.fv_fisherman_day_bring.1: I'm bringing the pot for the soup. Let those who bragged about their catch bring the fish.
line.town.fv_fisherman_day_grump.1: Today everyone's pike was this big. Ask tomorrow and it's half the length.
line.town.fv_fisherman_day_kid.1: We're fishing with bread off the pier. Whoever catches first doesn't wash the pot.
line.town.fv_fisherman_day_elder.1: The nets dried all along the promenade. We children ran under them as under a roof.
line.town.fv_perseids_bring.1: I'm taking two blankets and thyme tea. Stars are best watched lying down and warm.
line.town.fv_perseids_grump.1: My neck is stiff and only three fell. And those while I was pouring tea.
line.town.fv_perseids_kid.1: We're counting who sees the most. Aeroplanes don't count, I checked.
line.town.fv_perseids_elder.1: For the meteor shower we climbed the bathhouse roof. Many wishes, one roof.
line.town.fv_harvest_fair_bring.1: I'm bringing a marrow. It outgrew the wheelbarrow, so the wheelbarrow comes too.
line.town.fv_harvest_fair_grump.1: The first prize goes to a pumpkin again. Has anyone ever said thank you for my garlic?
line.town.fv_harvest_fair_kid.1: We're guessing what the pumpkin weighs. The closest gets a toffee apple.
line.town.fv_harvest_fair_elder.1: We dug potatoes with the whole family then. The last sack was carried home like a banner.
line.town.fv_lunar_new_year_bring.1: I'm bringing dumplings, the whole stair made them. One hides a coin, chew with care.
line.town.fv_lunar_new_year_grump.1: Firecrackers since morning. The cat has been under the bath for three hours.
line.town.fv_lunar_new_year_kid.1: We're following the dragon and counting its legs. I get a different number every time.
line.town.fv_lunar_new_year_elder.1: A neighbour from the fifth floor gave us red envelopes. Inside was a coin and a note: study.
line.town.fv_holi_bring.1: I'm bringing colours in paper cones. And an old shirt I won't miss.
line.town.fv_holi_grump.1: Fun for them. And I go about in green speckles for a week afterwards.
line.town.fv_holi_kid.1: Whoever stays clean longest loses. Those are the rules.
line.town.fv_holi_elder.1: We had no colours, we threw flour. Grandmother scolded us and laughed herself.
line.town.fv_nowruz_bring.1: I'm bringing sprouted wheat on a saucer. Two weeks of watering, it doesn't come greener.
line.town.fv_nowruz_grump.1: Seven dishes on the table, all starting with one letter. And what letter is the washing-up?
line.town.fv_nowruz_kid.1: We jump over the little fire. They won't let us over the big one yet.
line.town.fv_nowruz_elder.1: My mother put a mirror on the table and said: let the year see itself handsome.
line.town.fv_children_day_bring.1: I'm bringing chalk, about ten boxes. There's asphalt enough in town for everybody.
line.town.fv_children_day_grump.1: Children's day. As if the other three hundred and sixty-four weren't theirs.
line.town.fv_children_day_kid.1: Today we're drawing the longest snake in town. It's already gone round the corner.
line.town.fv_children_day_elder.1: On this day we got ice cream in a wafer cup. I ate so slowly that it ran away.
line.town.fv_tanabata_bring.1: I'm bringing coloured paper and thread. The town has many wishes, we need strips to spare.
line.town.fv_tanabata_grump.1: All the wishes hang in plain sight. I write mine small and hang it high.
line.town.fv_tanabata_kid.1: We read other people's wishes and guess whose they are. The bicycle one is Petya's for sure.
line.town.fv_tanabata_elder.1: I wish for the same thing every year. So far it comes true.
line.town.fv_toro_nagashi_bring.1: I'm bringing a lantern and matches. The name on it I write by hand, every year.
line.town.fv_toro_nagashi_grump.1: I don't like noise here. Tonight by the water one should keep quiet.
line.town.fv_toro_nagashi_kid.1: We watch whose lantern floats farthest. But you have to cheer in a whisper.
line.town.fv_toro_nagashi_elder.1: I set two lanterns on the water. One for my father, one for his boat.
line.town.fv_mid_autumn_bring.1: I'm bringing mooncakes. We'll cut them for everyone, a slice each, as is proper.
line.town.fv_mid_autumn_grump.1: A moon like any moon. It was rounder last year, I remember.
line.town.fv_mid_autumn_kid.1: We're looking for the hare on the moon. I can only see an ear, but it's a hare's for sure.
line.town.fv_mid_autumn_elder.1: Under such a moon we carried the table into the yard. The tea went cold and nobody wanted to leave.
line.town.fv_halloween_bring.1: I'm bringing a pumpkin with a face cut in it. It came out more surprised than scary.
line.town.fv_halloween_grump.1: The doorbell for the third time tonight. The sweets ran out at the second.
line.town.fv_halloween_kid.1: I'm a ghost. They let me take the sheet but not cut holes, so I can't see a thing.
line.town.fv_halloween_elder.1: We scared each other with a beetroot and a candle inside. The pumpkins were for jam.
line.town.fv_dia_de_muertos_bring.1: I'm bringing marigolds and bread. And grandfather's photograph, he liked a crowd.
line.town.fv_dia_de_muertos_grump.1: How merry they are. I say remembering is done quietly and over tea.
line.town.fv_dia_de_muertos_kid.1: We put a sweet on the little table for great-grandmother. She liked toffees, I asked.
line.town.fv_dia_de_muertos_elder.1: The older I get, the longer my list of people to remember. And the merrier the table, oddly.
line.town.fv_diwali_bring.1: I'm bringing clay lamps and oil. We'll stand them on every windowsill, as far as they go.
line.town.fv_diwali_grump.1: A light in every window. Pretty, but I don't envy the firemen tonight.
line.town.fv_diwali_kid.1: We're drawing a pattern by the door in coloured sand. The main thing is that nobody sneezes.
line.town.fv_diwali_elder.1: A neighbour taught us to light the lamps. Since then our stair is always bright this evening.
line.town.fv_loy_krathong_bring.1: I'm bringing a little boat of leaves. Burdock instead of banana, it floats just as well.
line.town.fv_loy_krathong_grump.1: They launch them and launch them. And who fishes them out tomorrow, the river king?
line.town.fv_loy_krathong_kid.1: I put a coin and a button in my boat. The coin for a wish, the button just because.
line.town.fv_loy_krathong_elder.1: As children we floated wood chips with candle stubs down the brook. We never knew it was a holiday.
line.town.fv_christmas_bring.1: I'm bringing the wheat pudding and a poppy-seed pie. Bring your own spoons, mine won't go round.
line.town.fv_christmas_grump.1: They dressed the tree in November. By the holiday nobody looks at it any more.
line.town.fv_christmas_kid.1: We're watching for the first star. Until it comes out nobody may touch the pie.
line.town.fv_christmas_elder.1: We went down the whole street with a star. We sang badly but loudly, and they gave us gingerbread.
line.town.fv_sun_day_bring.1: I'm bringing pancakes to the square. Round and yellow, as the day demands.
line.town.fv_sun_day_grump.1: Heat, a crowd, and everyone looking up. If only one of them looked where he walks.
line.town.fv_sun_day_kid.1: We're measuring whose shadow is shortest at noon. Mine has nearly gone!
line.town.fv_sun_day_elder.1: On Big Sun Day mother put every pillow out on the balcony. So we'd sleep bright all year, she said.
line.town.fv_city_day_bring.1: I'm bringing an album of old photographs. Let the young see where the stop used to be.
line.town.fv_city_day_grump.1: Speeches, speeches. Better if they'd mended the lamp on our street for the holiday.
line.town.fv_city_day_kid.1: We're looking for our houses in the old pictures. Ours turned up, only the tree beside it is tiny.
line.town.fv_city_day_elder.1: I remember when there was one pier here and three houses. And there was already a queue for bread.
line.town.fv_kite_day_bring.1: I'm bringing a kite and a ball of string. The tail is tied from old neckties, it flies with dignity.
line.town.fv_kite_day_grump.1: Half the sky is strings. Even the gulls go round.
line.town.fv_kite_day_kid.1: Whoever's kite is highest is the boss. Mine is caught in a poplar for now, but that's temporary.
line.town.fv_kite_day_elder.1: We glued our kites from newspaper with potato paste. They flew off news and all.
line.town.fv_cat_day_bring.1: I'm taking a saucer of sour cream to the door. Today the yard cats are owed a treat.
line.town.fv_cat_day_grump.1: Cat day. For my cat, by the way, it lasts all year.
line.town.fv_cat_day_kid.1: We're counting cats on windowsills. Ginger ones are worth two points.
line.town.fv_cat_day_elder.1: A cat called Mukha lived in our yard. She walked all the children to school and came back alone.
line.town.fv_book_day_bring.1: I'm bringing a pile of books to swap. Honestly read, with bookmarks and crumbs.
line.town.fv_book_day_grump.1: You give away a good book and get a handbook on land drainage in return.
line.town.fv_book_day_kid.1: We open a book anywhere and read the first line. The funniest one picks the next book.
line.town.fv_book_day_elder.1: I got my first book in exchange for a penknife. I missed the knife later, the book never.
line.town.fv_amber_morning_bring.1: I'm taking a sieve and rubber boots. After a storm the amber lies right at the water's edge.
line.town.fv_amber_morning_grump.1: The whole town on the shore since dawn. All that's left for me is seaweed.
line.town.fv_amber_morning_kid.1: Whoever finds amber with a fly inside wins for ever. I found one with a bubble.
line.town.fv_amber_morning_elder.1: After a storm grandmother woke us before dawn. The sea gives by night, she said, and grudges by day.
line.town.beach_castle_kid.1: I'm digging the moat! The moat is the most important part.
line.town.beach_castle_kid.2: The sand has to be wet. Dry sand just falls apart.
line.town.beach_castle_kid.3: Let's do one more tower, over there, at the edge.
line.town.beach_castle_kid.4: A wave's coming soon. Build faster!
line.town.beach_castle_kid.5: I'll stick shells on the wall. It'll be pretty.
line.town.beach_castle_kid.6: Have you got a flag? A castle without a flag doesn't count.
line.town.beach_castle_mind.1: The third castle this morning. The sea's winning so far.
line.town.beach_castle_mind.2: Don't go far from the water! And don't go close to it either.
line.town.beach_race_talk.1: The summer folk are racing to the buoy again. The lifeguard times every one of them.
line.town.beach_race_talk.2: The one in the white cap is first every summer. They say she swam for the town when she was young.
line.town.beach_race_talk.3: There's a new name on the lifeguard's sign. I wonder whose.
line.town.cruise_board.1: The Polden's launch leaves from the end of the pier. Ticket in my pocket, suitcase at my foot.
line.town.cruise_board.2: Two days without the vegetable patch. Hard to believe.
line.town.cruise_board.3: There she lies in the roads, all white. The funnel with the sun on it.
line.town.cruise_board.4: My neighbour asked for a postcard of the Far Light. I mustn't forget.
line.town.cruise_board_hero.1: For the Polden too? Then we'll meet at dinner.
line.town.cruise_board_hero.2: Don't be late: three blasts at six and the gangway comes up.
line.town.cruise_settle.1: The cabin is small and the window is round. Just as it should be.
line.town.cruise_settle.2: The upper berth or the lower? The eternal question.
line.town.cruise_settle.3: Suitcase under the berth, hat on the hook. Home already.
line.town.cruise_settle.4: The life jacket is in the locker. I hope it stays there.
line.town.cruise_departure.1: Three blasts. Now we really are sailing.
line.town.cruise_departure.2: Look, the promenade is like a toy already.
line.town.cruise_departure.3: I'll wave to my balcony. The cat may be watching.
line.town.cruise_departure.4: Leaving is jollier to a march. Even from a wheezy loudspeaker.
line.town.cruise_drill.1: Boat number two, port side. To be remembered like my own address.
line.town.cruise_drill.2: The bosun talks so they can hear him on shore.
line.town.cruise_drill.3: The jacket ties at the front. Mine came out as a bow.
line.town.cruise_drill.4: A practice alarm, and the heart beats for real.
line.town.cruise_dinner.1: The soup rocks in the bowl along with the ship. One has to eat faster.
line.town.cruise_dinner.2: Everyone at our table is from the same town, and we only meet here.
line.town.cruise_dinner.3: A starched cloth, a napkin folded like a swan. A pity to unfold it.
line.town.cruise_dinner.4: The captain sits at that table over there. He eats like anybody else.
line.town.cruise_breakfast.1: Porridge on a ship tastes better than at home. The air, I suppose.
line.town.cruise_breakfast.2: Something knocked softly under the floor at night. The engine, they say.
line.town.cruise_breakfast.3: Tea in a glass holder, and not a drop spilt. That is experience for you.
line.town.cruise_lunch.1: Borscht, a cutlet, compote. At sea they have other names, but the taste is the same.
line.town.cruise_lunch.2: In the fresh air one has a sailor's appetite.
line.town.cruise_lunch.3: The cook looked out of the hatch: checking that the plates were clean.
line.town.cruise_tea.1: They serve little ring biscuits with the tea. Sea ones, I suppose.
line.town.cruise_tea.2: Tea at four, the lighthouse at half past. A timetable like at a station.
line.town.cruise_tea.3: My third glass. At sea, tea is meant to take a long time.
line.town.cruise_gala.1: The captain's dinner. A good thing there was an ironed shirt in the suitcase.
line.town.cruise_gala.2: The band plays softly, so you can hear the forks ring.
line.town.cruise_gala.3: The captain said three words and everybody stood up. Now that is a toast.
line.town.cruise_isl_brothers.1: The Stone Brothers. Three stacks, and the sun sets exactly between them.
line.town.cruise_isl_brothers.2: The youngest brother leans right over. Tired of standing.
line.town.cruise_isl_brothers.3: You can't see them from the shore. Worth sailing for this alone.
line.town.cruise_isl_arch.1: The Needle's Eye at sunrise. For this one gets up even at five.
line.town.cruise_isl_arch.2: The sun went through the arch like a thread through a needle.
line.town.cruise_isl_birds.1: Bird Island. The cliffs are white, and that is not snow.
line.town.cruise_isl_birds.2: They scream so loud you can't hear the ship's horn.
line.town.cruise_isl_birds.3: The Japanese guest looks through his telescope and writes. Every single bird, I suppose.
line.town.cruise_isl_birds.4: Better hold on to your hat. And not only against the wind.
line.town.cruise_isl_lighthouse.1: The Far Light. A bare rock, a tower and one garden of three beds.
line.town.cruise_isl_lighthouse.2: Somebody is waving from the gallery. Let's wave back, he'll be glad.
line.town.cruise_isl_lighthouse.3: At night you can see its light from the cabin. Count the flashes and fall asleep.
line.town.cruise_isl_seals.1: The Seal Rocks. That rock over there just yawned.
line.town.cruise_isl_seals.2: They lie and look at us. It's an outing for them too.
line.town.cruise_isl_seals.3: Hush, don't scare them. Though I don't think they care.
line.town.cruise_isl_home.1: There's our cable car. From here the cabins are like beads.
line.town.cruise_isl_home.2: You wouldn't know your own town from the sea. A handsome one, it turns out.
line.town.cruise_isl_home.3: Two days, and it feels like a month.
line.town.cruise_rail.1: The water astern is like lace. One could watch it for an hour.
line.town.cruise_rail.2: A gull has been following us from the roads. Waiting for lunch.
line.town.cruise_rail.3: No shore on either side. Now this is the sea.
line.town.cruise_rail.4: The rail is warm from the sun.
line.town.cruise_rail_night.1: So many stars that the navigator must find it hard to choose.
line.town.cruise_rail_night.2: The water is black at night, and the wake behind us glows.
line.town.cruise_deck_walk.1: Seven turns round the deck make a kilometre. The entertainer said so.
line.town.cruise_deck_walk.2: I walk straight, and the deck walks a little sideways.
line.town.cruise_deck_walk.3: The sailors are painting something white white.
line.town.cruise_deckchair.1: A deck chair, a rug and the horizon. Nothing else is needed.
line.town.cruise_deckchair.2: The book is open at the same page as yesterday.
line.town.cruise_deckchair.3: My eyes close by themselves. It's all the sea air.
line.town.cruise_deckchair.4: The funnel overhead hums softly, like a big kettle.
line.town.cruise_exercise.1: Exercises at a quarter past seven. On deck, in the wind. It wakes you up.
line.town.cruise_exercise.2: With the ship rolling, the bends do themselves.
line.town.cruise_exercise.3: One-two, three-four. At home one would never be up so early.
line.town.cruise_deckgames.1: You throw the rings over a peg. So far they all fly off to the lifeboat.
line.town.cruise_deckgames.2: Deck shuffleboard. Easier than the word for it.
line.town.cruise_deckgames.3: Our team is called the Anchor. Because it drags us to the bottom.
line.town.cruise_concert.1: The quartet plays what they played at the dance floor when we were young.
line.town.cruise_concert.2: The double bass is bigger than its player. How does he carry it up the ladders?
line.town.cruise_concert.3: They play well. And the floor sways in time.
line.town.cruise_concert.4: The newlyweds dance as if there were nobody else here.
line.town.cruise_dance.1: A waltz on a ship: the step is yours, the sea does the turn.
line.town.cruise_dance.2: The feet remember. The head no longer does, but the feet remember.
line.town.cruise_dance.3: One more dance and then bed. That's the third time now.
line.town.cruise_quiz.1: How many knots in a mile? None, they're different things. But a sly question.
line.town.cruise_quiz.2: I can answer about the islands. About sailor's knots, no.
line.town.cruise_quiz.3: The prize is a paper boat with a stamp on it. I want one.
line.town.cruise_diplomas.1: A seafarer's diploma. It will hang over my desk, next to the one for cucumbers.
line.town.cruise_diplomas.2: The captain's signature is real, in ink.
line.town.cruise_diplomas.3: They call you by your surname, as at school. And it's just as frightening.
line.town.cruise_saloon.1: The saloon armchairs are such that you don't want to get up before we land.
line.town.cruise_saloon.2: The barman remembers what everybody ordered yesterday. What a memory.
line.town.cruise_saloon.3: The lemonade here has bigger bubbles than ashore.
line.town.cruise_library.1: The ship's library is all about the sea. And one handbook on beekeeping.
line.town.cruise_library.2: Quiet, only the clock and the engine.
line.town.cruise_cards.1: The engineer from Riga is lucky again tonight. The third evening running.
line.town.cruise_cards.2: We play for matches. There are no matches left.
line.town.cruise_smoke.1: At the stern the wind takes the smoke before you can draw on it.
line.town.cruise_smoke.2: Smoking only here. The bosun sees everything.
line.town.cruise_pack.1: The suitcase won't shut for some reason. And nothing was bought.
line.town.cruise_pack.2: The diploma on top, so it doesn't crease.
line.town.cruise_pack.3: A pity to leave the cabin. One gets used to it in two nights.
line.town.cruise_hello.1: Oh, you're here too! A fellow townsman at sea is nearly family.
line.town.cruise_hello.2: Well, how is your cabin? Our window is right over the water.
line.town.cruise_hello.3: Don't sleep through Bird Island tomorrow. They say it's the best of the trip.
line.town.cruise_hello.4: In town we greet each other every other time, and here we're like old friends.
line.town.cruise_hello_known.1: Neighbour! Sit with us later and tell what you saw from the bridge.
line.town.cruise_hello_known.2: I'll tell them at home that we sailed together. They won't believe it.
line.town.cruise_chat_deck.2: The main one. The window is at the water, the fish can see everything.
line.town.cruise_chat_deck.3: We're below. But you hear the engine like a heart.
line.town.cruise_chat_deck.4: Have you noticed? Nobody here looks at a clock.
line.town.cruise_chat_deck.5: Why would they? The loudspeaker calls you to lunch.
line.town.cruise_chat_table.1: Pass the bread, please. Before it travels off by itself.
line.town.cruise_chat_table.2: Here. When she rolls, the plates go visiting.
line.town.cruise_chat_table.3: We live across the yard from each other. And only got talking here.
line.town.cruise_chat_table.4: So we had to sail away first.
line.town.cruise_ev_island.1: An island to starboard! Everybody to the rail!
line.town.cruise_ev_island.2: There it is, coming up. First like a cloud, then like a stone.
line.town.cruise_ev_home.1: The anchor rattled down. So here we are.
line.town.cruise_ev_home.2: The launch is already coming for us. A pity it's so soon.
line.town.cook_shop_spring.1: The smelt is running! I'm frying tonight, the whole stairwell will smell of cucumber.
line.town.cook_shop_spring.2: Mustn't forget flour. You don't fry smelt without flour.
line.town.cook_shop_spring.3: The dill is still hothouse, weak stuff. Never mind, our own will be up soon.
line.town.cook_shop_summer.1: Two bottles of kefir: in this heat it's okroshka or nothing.
line.town.cook_shop_summer.2: Our own radishes, our own cucumbers, the kefir from the shop. Nearly all homemade.
line.town.cook_shop_summer.3: Sugar for jam, five kilos. The strawberries are better than ever this year.
line.town.cook_shop_summer.4: The grandchildren are coming, I'll bake them everything. If only the weather holds.
line.town.cook_shop_autumn.1: They brought Baltic herring in today, fresh. I'll boil it with jacket potatoes.
line.town.cook_shop_autumn.2: The potatoes are dug, so it's draniki till spring.
line.town.cook_shop_autumn.3: Out of jars for the winter. Need more, or the cucumbers will grow too big.
line.town.cook_shop_winter.1: I'll open a jar of jam for tea. Made in summer, remembered in winter.
line.town.cook_shop_winter.2: Some cod for ukha. In winter cod ukha is the best.
line.town.cook_home_table.1: Sit down, it'll go cold! The draniki are straight from the pan.
line.town.cook_home_table.2: Pass the salt. No, taste it first, then salt.
line.town.cook_home_table.3: Mother cooked it just like this. Nobody's invented anything better than home cooking.
line.town.cook_home_table.4: Whoever finishes last does the washing up. That's the law.
line.town.cook_home_kid.1: Carrot salad again? Well, all right, with apple it's fine.
line.town.cook_home_kid.2: Can I have the jam foam? Please!
line.town.cook_home_kid.3: They let me peel the potatoes! Well, nearly all of them.
line.town.fv_science_day_bring.1: I'm taking an oscilloscope to the fair. Let the children see what sound looks like.
line.town.fv_science_day_grump.1: Once a year the institute opens its doors, and at once there's a queue as if for oranges.
line.town.fv_science_day_kid.1: We're making a volcano out of soda. Whoever stands nearest goes and washes afterwards.
line.town.fv_science_day_elder.1: The first lecture on the square was given in a hard frost. Nobody left till it got to the Sun.
line.town.nh_sci_greet.1: Happy Science Day! The globe at the fair gives you a shock. Go on, it doesn't hurt.
line.town.nh_sci_greet.2: Happy Science Day! The quiz on the square is at half past four.
line.town.nh_sci.1: Today the institute has come out into the street. Tomorrow it shuts again and thinks.
line.town.nh_sci.2: They say everything they do in there is about the Sun. Even the canteen.
line.town.nh_sci.3: The oxygen cocktail is free. The queue for it does cost you: half an hour of your life.
line.town.nh_sci.4: At the blitz quiz the bell is what matters. Knowing the answer doesn't hurt either.
line.town.nh_sci_fair_kid.1: We're selling the potato cakes ourselves today. We do the change in a column!
line.town.nh_sci_fair_kid.2: Our club is saving for a telescope. We're a hundred and forty cakes short.
line.town.nh_sci_fair_vendor.1: Class 6B is behind the counter today, and I'm their cashier and their conscience.
line.town.nh_sci_fair_vendor.2: Who wants a cocktail of pure oxygen? It makes you cleverer right up till evening!
line.town.nh_sci_lecture.1: Hush, now comes the part about why it shines.
line.town.nh_sci_lecture.2: The light flies for eight minutes. And we stand waiting for it all winter.
line.town.nh_sci_quiz.1: I know the answer! I know it! No, I don't any more.
line.town.nh_sci_quiz.2: Our yard against the laboratory. So far the laboratory is losing to the caretaker.
line.town.nh_sci_stars.1: The queue for the telescope is longer than the one for the cocktail. So it's a proper town.
line.town.nh_sci_stars.2: That bright one isn't a star, it's a planet. I've just had it explained to me.
line.town.nh_sci_talk.1: Are you going to the lecture?
line.town.nh_sci_talk.2: To the lecture. And you, to the quiz?
line.town.nh_sci_talk.3: To the quiz. I'll answer with whatever I hear at your lecture.
line.town.fv_old_new_year_bring.1: Gingerbread and coins for the children: they'll come singing, and a house should give back.
line.town.fv_old_new_year_grump.1: We haven't finished eating the first New Year, and here's a second. No salad lives that long.
line.town.fv_old_new_year_kid.1: We carry the sun on a pole and sing. Whoever holds the sun gets double gingerbread!
line.town.fv_old_new_year_elder.1: The whole yard poured wax. One girl got a boat, and that summer she did sail off to be married.
line.town.nh_ony_greet.1: Happy Old New Year! Have you had a dumpling with a surprise yet?
line.town.nh_ony_greet.2: Happy old new one! Midnight at the tree, don't sleep through it a second time.
line.town.nh_ony.1: Well thought of: if you missed making a wish the first time, make it the second.
line.town.nh_ony.2: The tree stands its last night. Tomorrow all that's left is needles, right up to summer.
line.town.nh_ony.3: They're pouring wax at the dumpling bar tonight. I wonder how that went down in the books.
line.town.nh_ony_carols.1: Hear them singing? They're coming with the sun. Get the gingerbread ready.
line.town.nh_ony_carols.2: Elsewhere they carry a star. Here it's always the sun, and nobody asks why.
line.town.nh_ony_carols_kid.1: We sow, we strew, we scatter grain, and wish you joy of the sun again!
line.town.nh_ony_carols_kid.2: That entrance gave us three gingerbreads and an apple. Let's go again, with hats on!
line.town.nh_ony_carols_kid.3: My turn to carry the sun! You carried it from the post office to the fountain.
line.town.nh_ony_fortune.1: I'm throwing a felt boot. Whichever way the toe points, that's where the news will come from.
line.town.nh_ony_fortune.2: Ask the first passer-by their name. Only not the caretaker: everyone has asked him already.
line.town.nh_ony_fortune.3: The boot pointed out to sea. So it's a wait till spring.
line.town.nh_ony_midnight.1: The second time this winter that midnight is a real midnight, with the chimes.
line.town.nh_ony_midnight.2: Happy new old one! Now it's the new year for certain.
line.town.nh_ony_cook.1: Tonight every tenth dumpling has a surprise. The rest have cherries, as ever.
line.town.nh_ony_cook.2: We boil the buttons for the dumplings separately. We have a hygiene certificate.
line.town.nh_ony_talk.1: What did you get in your dumpling?
line.town.nh_ony_talk.3: From here? A long journey here is to the lighthouse and back.
line.town.fv_neptune_day_bring.1: I'm taking a dry towel for everyone to the beach, and one more to spare. I know this day.
line.town.fv_neptune_day_grump.1: They tip a bucket over you and say “happy holiday”. And a person has receipts in their pocket.
line.town.fv_neptune_day_kid.1: We're the devils! We smear soot on everyone who's dry. Haven't you been smeared yet?
line.town.fv_neptune_day_elder.1: Neptune was the tug's bosun then. His own beard, and a trident off a pitchfork, same as now.
line.town.nh_nep_greet.1: Happy Neptune Day! You look suspiciously dry.
line.town.nh_nep_greet.2: Happy Neptune Day! The boat parade is at three, best seen from the pier.
line.town.nh_nep.1: There's one law on the beach today: whoever is dry is in the wrong.
line.town.nh_nep.2: The inner tubes for the race went by morning. The last one, they say, is at the rental.
line.town.nh_nep.3: The lifeguards are making the fish soup. So nobody will drown, not even in the soup.
line.town.nh_nep_landing.1: He's coming! There's the loofah beard, there's the trident!
line.town.nh_nep_landing.2: Every year he walks out of the sea, and every year he asks who is in charge here.
line.town.nh_nep_court.1: Neptune judges quickly: guilty, duck him. Not guilty, duck him as well.
line.town.nh_nep_court.2: They're hauling our lot into the water on the rope. I'll go and help. The devils.
line.town.nh_nep_court_kid.1: I'm a mermaid! Mermaids may splash without asking.
line.town.nh_nep_court_kid.2: The soot's run out. We're smearing wet sand now, it's even better.
line.town.nh_nep_parade.1: The boat with Neptune goes first. The devils are rowing, which is why it's crooked.
line.town.nh_nep_parade.2: Count the boats. Last year there were eleven and one air mattress.
line.town.nh_nep_ukha.1: Everyone brings their catch for the common pot. Whoever caught nothing brings a bay leaf.
line.town.nh_nep_ukha.2: Take any bowl. Today the soup is nobody's and everybody's.
line.town.nh_nep_lifeguard.1: Two of us on duty today: one watches the water, the other stirs the soup.
line.town.nh_nep_lifeguard.2: No swimming past the buoys! That goes for Neptune too.
line.town.nh_nep_talk.2: Twice. The second time by mistake.
line.town.nh_nep_talk.3: Neptune makes no mistakes. So there was a reason.
line.town.soda_kid.3: If you tie the coin to a string, does it come back?
line.town.soda_kid.4: It's cherry today. Yesterday it was tarragon, the green one.
line.town.soda_grown.1: Rinse the glass, don't be lazy. There's only the one for all of us.
line.town.soda_grown.2: Plain is even better. Cold and prickly.
line.town.soda_grown.3: It swallowed the coin again. You knock it on the side, right here.
line.town.soda_grown.4: In this heat only soda water saves you.
line.town.soda_grown.5: The syrup's a bit thin today. They're skimping.
line.town.soda_elder.1: They used to chain the glass on. People took it anyway.
line.town.soda_elder.2: Once you got two glasses for a coin like this.
line.town.street_kvass_vendor.1: Cold kvass, from the barrel! A small mug, a big mug!
line.town.street_kvass_vendor.2: Brought a can? I'll fill it to the brim.
line.town.street_kvass_vendor.3: The barrel will be dry by lunch. Latecomers miss out.
line.town.street_kvass_vendor.4: A queue, citizens, a queue. There's kvass for everyone who stands in it.
line.town.street_kvass_vendor.5: Such heat, and the barrel still cold. That's what I call a barrel.
line.town.street_kvass_vendor_near.1: Young man, a mug? In this heat it's a sin to walk past.
line.town.street_kvass_vendor_near.2: Come up, don't be shy. The kvass won't drink itself.
line.town.street_icecream_vendor.2: The eskimo's running out. Take one while there are some.
line.town.street_icecream_vendor.3: Don't drop it, don't drop it! Well, there. Take a new one, that one's for the gulls.
line.town.street_icecream_vendor.4: The cart's like a fridge, and I'm next to it like on a frying pan.
line.town.street_icecream_vendor_near.2: Plombir for you, or an eskimo? I can see by your eyes it's plombir.
line.town.street_kvass_buyer.1: A big one, please. No, two small ones instead.
line.town.street_kvass_buyer.2: Oof, ice cold. Goes right to the back of the head.
line.town.street_kvass_buyer.3: Kvass from the barrel and kvass from a bottle are two different lives.
line.town.street_icecream_kid.1: An eskimo for me! No, fruit ice! No, eskimo!
line.town.street_icecream_kid.2: If you eat it fast your head rings.
line.town.street_icecream_kid.3: Mum gave me enough for one. I'll share. Maybe.
line.town.street_icecream_kid.4: It's already running down my hand, and that was only the first bite.
line.town.street_icecream_grown.1: Plombir at twenty-eight. I remember when it was twenty.
line.town.street_icecream_grown.2: One plombir, please. For me. Not for a child, for me.
line.town.street_sweep.1: While the town sleeps, the street is mine.
line.town.street_sweep.2: Sunflower husks by the benches again. Every evening, husks.
line.town.street_sweep.3: A birch broom, home made. Shop ones don't sweep like this.
line.town.street_sweep.4: The gulls dragged it all here overnight, and I clean it up.
line.town.street_sweep_near.1: An early bird. Go round, it's dusty here.
line.town.street_sweep_near.2: Lift your feet, young man, or I'll sweep you up too.
line.town.street_milk.1: Milk, sour cream, curd! Bring out your cans!
line.town.street_milk.2: The third entrance overslept again. I'll leave it at the door.
line.town.street_milk.3: This morning's, still warm. The evening's will be tomorrow.
line.town.street_milk.4: Don't forget the empty bottles, I have to hand them in.
line.town.street_shutters.2: The shutter squeaks again. Needs oiling. Every morning it needs oiling.
line.town.street_shutters.3: By the time it's swept and we're open, there's the first customer.
line.town.street_hang_laundry.1: Sun, a breeze, it'll all be dry by lunch.
line.town.street_hang_laundry.2: Where are the pegs? The children took them again.
line.town.street_hang_laundry.3: The sheets on the far line, the sun stays longer there.
line.town.street_hang_laundry.4: Dry it by the sea and it smells of the sea. Better than any powder.
line.town.street_take_laundry.1: Clouds coming in from the sea. Take it in, take it in, quickly!
line.town.street_take_laundry.2: One more hour and it'd be dry. Never mind, it'll finish at home.
line.town.street_take_laundry.4: Smells of the sun. That's why I like drying it in the yard.
line.town.street_grannies.1: The Petrovs have guests again. Third time this week.
line.town.street_grannies.2: My blood pressure's jumping today. The weather's changing, mark my words.
line.town.street_grannies.3: My grandson called. Promised to come. In summer. Which summer, he didn't say.
line.town.street_grannies.4: In the old days there was order in the yard. Though it's not bad now either.
line.town.street_grannies.5: Sit, sit, where's the hurry. It's sunny.
line.town.street_grannies_near.1: Who's that? Not one of ours, it seems.
line.town.street_grannies_near.2: Hello, dear. Whose are you, then?
line.town.street_grannies_near.3: So thin. Do they feed you over there, or not?
line.town.street_grannies_near.4: You should put a hat on. The wind's off the sea, you'll catch a chill.
line.town.street_yard_dominoes.1: Blocked! Count them up, Mikhalych, count.
line.town.street_yard_dominoes.2: Don't slam them so, the whole yard can hear.
line.town.street_yard_dominoes.3: One more game while it's light.
line.town.street_yard_dominoes.4: My grandfather knocked this table together. And lost at it too.
line.town.street_yard_dominoes.5: Double blank. Your go, if you've got anything.
line.town.street_rake_leaves.1: You rake them up, and the wind scatters them back. That's life.
line.town.street_rake_leaves.2: The maple shed early this year. Winter will come early.
line.town.street_rake_leaves.3: Kids, leave the pile alone! Well, all right, you can have one.
line.town.street_rake_leaves.4: Leaves smell of autumn. Nothing else smells like that.
line.town.street_subbotnik_paint.1: A green bench, as always. We never have any other paint.
line.town.street_subbotnik_paint.2: Don't sit! Wet paint! Someone write a sign.
line.town.street_subbotnik_paint.3: One brush for three of us, but paint enough for ten.
line.town.street_subbotnik_whitewash.1: Whitewash up to the waist, evenly. Like the neighbours', only better.
line.town.street_subbotnik_whitewash.2: Don't splash lime in your eyes, keep the bucket lower.
line.town.street_subbotnik_whitewash.3: The trees in white knee socks: spring has come.
line.town.street_subbotnik_sweep.1: The whole yard came out. Even the fifth floor came down.
line.town.street_subbotnik_sweep.2: Tea at Zinaida's after the subbotnik. She promised a pie.
line.town.street_subbotnik_sweep.3: Last year's leaves came out from under the snow. Raking.
line.town.street_subbotnik_near.1: Subbotnik! The rakes are over there, grab one and join in.
line.town.street_subbotnik_near.2: Don't stand there like a post, lad. At least hold a bucket.
line.town.days_cold.1: My throat's raw. To the clinic, then straight home.
line.town.days_cold.2: Don't come close, you'll catch it. Second day of this cold.
line.town.days_cold.3: Raspberry tea, a blanket, and no walks at all.
line.town.days_cold.4: Achoo! So much for the sea air.
line.town.days_cold_kid.1: I've got a temperature. No school for me!
line.town.days_cold_kid.2: Mum says my throat's red. I'll be at home watching cartoons.
line.town.days_sleepy.1: Tossing and turning all night, and then the alarm at dawn.
line.town.days_sleepy.3: The gulls were screaming from four in the morning. Some sleep that was.
line.town.days_sleepy.4: I'm late. Third time this month, honestly.
line.town.days_sleepy.5: I'll lie down for half an hour this afternoon. I won't last till evening otherwise.
line.town.days_birthday.1: It's my birthday today. Guests tonight, I must get the cake in time.
line.town.days_birthday.2: Another year. And the sea's still the same, thank goodness.
line.town.days_birthday.3: Three cards in the letterbox already this morning. They remember!
line.town.days_birthday_kid.1: It's my birthday! There'll be a cake with candles!
line.town.days_birthday_kid.2: My friends are coming over today. Guess how old I am!
line.town.days_guest.1: Off to a birthday. Here's the present, and nobody signed the card.
line.town.days_guest.2: As long as I'm not late for the cake.
line.town.days_guest.3: Flowers or a book for a birthday? I'm bringing both.
line.town.days_payday.1: Payday! We're not eating at home tonight.
line.town.days_payday.2: Once a fortnight you can have a pastry with your coffee.
line.town.days_payday.3: We've been paid. It'll be gone by Monday, but today we've been paid.
line.town.days_payday.4: Debts first, then the café. Or the other way round?
line.town.days_pension.1: It's pension day. There's a queue at the office from nine, best go early.
line.town.days_pension.2: I'll collect it and go to the market. Sweets for the grandchildren, herring for me.
line.town.days_pension.3: On pension day our whole house stands in one queue.
line.town.days_pension.4: It isn't much, but it's on time. Every second Wednesday.
line.town.days_market.1: Saturday means the market. The early ones get the curd cheese.
line.town.days_market.2: The fishermen bring it fresh on Saturdays. I buy for the whole week.
line.town.days_market.3: A long list and one bag. As always.
line.town.days_market.4: You hear all the news at the market sooner than in the paper.
line.town.days_library.1: Taking the books back. They were due yesterday, I hope I won't get told off.
line.town.days_library.2: Read them. Now I'll take something thicker.
line.town.days_library.3: It's my library day. Once a week, like clockwork.
line.town.days_tea.1: I'm going visiting, for tea. Can't come empty-handed, so here, gingerbread.
line.town.days_tea.2: I was asked for five. I'll come at half past, like all decent people.
line.town.days_tea.3: We'll sit in the kitchen and talk. Haven't met for ages, a whole week.
line.town.days_family.1: To the old folks' for Sunday dinner. There's a pie, no refusing.
line.town.days_family.2: Sunday is the law with us: the whole family at one table.
line.town.days_family.3: They'll say again that we hardly ever come. And we come every week.
line.town.days_family_kid.1: We're going to Granny's! She's got pancakes and a cat.
line.town.days_family_kid.2: Grandpa has a real compass. He promised to show me.
line.town.days_stroll.1: In the evening we always walk to the pier and back.
line.town.days_stroll.2: Look at that sky. Worth coming out for.
line.town.days_stroll.3: Don't hurry. We're out for a walk, we're not late.
line.town.days_stroll.4: Take my arm. There's a wind off the sea.
line.town.days_stroll_talk1.1: Remember the first time we walked here?
line.town.days_stroll_talk1.2: I do. It was raining, and we had one umbrella.
line.town.days_stroll_talk1.3: We still have just the one.
line.town.days_stroll_talk2.1: Shall we go as far as the lamp and turn back?
line.town.days_stroll_talk2.2: To the pier. Tonight, to the pier.
line.town.days_chess.1: So... If the knight goes here, the bishop is left unguarded.
line.town.days_chess.2: We've been finishing this game for three weeks now.
line.town.days_chess_talk1.2: I can see. Don't rush me.
line.town.days_chess_talk2.1: Move, will you. The sun will go down.
line.town.days_chess_talk3.2: Never. Tomorrow, on this same bench.
line.town.days_meet1.1: Oh, hello! Where are you off to?
line.town.days_meet1.2: Just errands. And I haven't seen you for ages.
line.town.days_meet1.3: Drop in for tea some time.
line.town.days_meet2.1: Wait, wait. Any word on tomorrow's weather?
line.town.days_meet2.2: They say the wind will change.
line.town.days_meet2.3: Then I'm not hanging the washing out today.
line.town.days_meet3.2: Still going strong. And your people?
line.town.days_meet4.1: I was just thinking of you, and here you are.
line.town.days_meet4.2: It's a small town. Everybody here thinks of everybody.
line.town.days_meet5.1: Are you going to the market on Saturday?
line.town.days_meet5.2: I am. I'll keep you a place in the queue for curd cheese.
line.town.days_meet5.3: That's what I like about you. Well, I must run.
line.town.days_nod.4: Oh, you're here too. My respects.
line.town.days_nod.5: Hi! I'll tell you later, I'm in a rush.
line.town.days_nod_morning.1: Good morning! Up and about already?
line.town.days_nod_morning.2: Good morning! The bread is in, the van is at the bakery.
line.town.days_nod_evening.1: Good evening! Lovely tonight, isn't it?
line.town.days_nod_evening.2: Evening. Give my regards to your family.
line.town.days_door.1: Go on, go on. I've got the door.
line.town.days_door.2: After you. I'm in no hurry.
line.town.days_door.3: Come in, the spring on this one is stiff.
line.town.tc_hello.1: Hello. Was there something you wanted to ask?
line.town.tc_hello_morning.2: Morning. The town's only just waking up.
line.town.tc_hello_evening.1: Good evening. A walk before bed?
line.town.tc_hello_evening.2: Evening! Lovely out just now, isn't it?
line.town.tc_hello_night.1: It's late. Why aren't you asleep?
line.town.tc_hello_night.2: The middle of the night and you're out walking. Well, hello.
line.town.tc_hello_rain.1: Hello! It's pouring. Out with it before we both dissolve.
line.town.tc_hello_snow.1: Hello! Look at that snow, eh? So, what is it?
line.town.tc_hello_cold.1: Hello. Don't stand still, you'll freeze. What is it?
line.town.tc_hello_new_elder.1: Hello, lad. Whose boy are you?
line.town.tc_hello_new.1: Hello. I don't think we've met?
line.town.tc_hello_known.2: Hello! Everybody round here knows you by now.
line.town.tc_hello_friendly.1: Oh, hi! I was just thinking about you.
line.town.tc_hello_friendly.2: Hi! I've a minute, let's chat.
line.town.tc_hello_friend.1: Fancy meeting you, {0}! So, how are you?
line.town.tc_hello_friend.2: Hi, {0}! Come here and tell me everything.
line.town.tc_hello_friend.3: I've been waiting for you, {0}! Sit down and tell me everything.
line.town.tc_hello_kid.2: Hi. You're from that club, aren't you?
line.town.tc_hello_elder.1: Hello, dear. Come closer, my hearing's not what it was.
line.town.tc_hello_elder.2: Hello, hello. It's nice when young people say hello.
line.town.tc_hello_work.1: Hello! Nobody's waiting, so ask away.
line.town.tc_hello_work.2: Good day. I've got a minute.
line.town.tc_hello_sit.1: Hello. Sit down, no sense standing.
line.town.tc_bye.2: All the best! Don't be a stranger.
line.town.tc_bye_evening.1: Good night. Don't stay out too late.
line.town.tc_bye_evening.2: Have a good evening! Mind your step, it's getting dark.
line.town.tc_bye_rain.1: Run along before you're soaked through!
line.town.tc_bye_cold.1: Go and get warm. And put a hat on!
line.town.tc_bye_friendly.1: That was a good chat. Come again!
line.town.tc_bye_kid.1: Bye! I've still got playing to do.
line.town.tc_bye_elder.1: Off you go, bless you. And eat properly.
line.town.tc_bye_work.1: Right, back to work for me. Drop in!
line.town.tc_bye_new.1: Now we know each other. Look in some time.
line.town.tc_no_work.1: Just a moment, I've a customer.
line.town.tc_no_work.2: Not now. See, people are waiting.
line.town.tc_no_work.3: Work first. Come back a bit later.
line.town.tc_no_hurry.2: No time, no time! Must run!
line.town.tc_no_hurry.3: We'll talk later, all right? I'm running late.
line.town.tc_no_shy.1: Mum says not to talk to strangers.
line.town.tc_no_shy.3: Who are you? I'd better go.
line.town.tc_work.2: Ticking along. Something new every day.
line.town.tc_work_pensioner.1: In retirement the main job is not to hurry. I manage.
line.town.tc_work_pensioner.2: My blood pressure's up and down, otherwise mustn't grumble.
line.town.tc_work_pensioner.3: Getting along. Market in the morning, bench by day, tea at night.
line.town.tc_work_pensioner.4: Forty years of work behind me. Now my shift is feeding pigeons.
line.town.tc_work_pupil.1: Fine. Top marks in maths; don't ask about singing.
line.town.tc_work_pupil.2: We've a poem to learn. It's as long as the promenade.
line.town.tc_work_pupil.3: Roll on the holidays. I'll live on the beach all summer.
line.town.tc_work_pupil.4: We've a new teacher. Strict, but she lets us draw.
line.town.tc_work_student.1: Exams any day now and here I am chatting. Bliss.
line.town.tc_work_student.2: The term paper won't write itself. A week of testing proves it.
line.town.tc_work_away.1: I work out of town, on the road every day. Coming back is the good part.
line.town.tc_work_away.2: Off in the morning, back by evening. I mostly see the town at dusk.
line.town.tc_work_researcher.1: We count, we measure, we argue. Science is mostly arguing.
line.town.tc_work_researcher.2: The experiment disagreed again. So there'll be something to tell.
line.town.tc_work_researcher.3: In Academgorodok we say: if it all makes sense, you didn't look hard enough.
line.town.tc_work_fisherman.1: The sea feeds you, on its own timetable. Not generous today.
line.town.tc_work_fisherman.2: Nets whole, engine pulling, wind not cross. What more could a fisherman ask?
line.town.tc_work_fisherman.3: The fish are running. Come to the pier towards evening and see.
line.town.tc_work_writer.1: Writing. A page yesterday, a comma today. But what a comma!
line.town.tc_work_writer.2: The novel's stuck. I walk the town eavesdropping for plots.
line.town.tc_work_seller.1: Trade's steady. Bread goes in the morning, gossip by evening.
line.town.tc_work_seller.2: Customers are choosy these days. But everyone says hello.
line.town.tc_work_seller.3: On my feet all day, they ache. But it's dull without people.
line.town.tc_work_programmer.1: Fixing what broke in my own hands yesterday. Business as usual.
line.town.tc_work_programmer.2: The program works. Nobody knows why. We don't touch it.
line.town.tc_work_station.1: The cable car runs, the coffee brews. Passengers are sleepy but polite.
line.town.tc_work_station.2: All day at the station. Cabins go back and forth, I stay put.
line.town.tc_work_homemaker.1: Home is a job too, only with no days off and no bonus.
line.town.tc_work_homemaker.2: Soup's on, washing's drying. Five minutes of quiet, then back.
line.town.tc_work_musician.1: Rehearsing. The neighbours know the programme by heart already.
line.town.tc_work_musician.2: There's music and there's a hall. Come and listen at the culture house.
line.town.tc_work_unemployed.1: Looking for work. So far I've found only the sea and spare time.
line.town.tc_work_unemployed.2: Nothing yet. But I know the town better than any postman.
line.town.tc_work_artist.1: The light's good today. That's all the work needs.
line.town.tc_work_artist.2: Third day painting the same fence. It's worth it.
line.town.tc_work_cook.1: The kitchen's been at it since morning. Soup by lunch, drop in.
line.town.tc_work_cook.2: The guests are fed, the tips are modest. One gets by.
line.town.tc_work_office.1: Paper, paper. By evening even the people rustle.
line.town.tc_work_office.2: Lots of work, but good people. That's the main thing.
line.town.tc_work_guest.1: Resting! Treatments, walks, fruit kissel. I don't want to go home.
line.town.tc_work_guest.2: The air here: you could bottle it.
line.town.tc_work_keeper.1: A quiet watch. A quiet watch is a good watch.
line.town.tc_work_keeper.2: Keeping things in order. The town won't sweep itself.
line.town.tc_day.1: A day like any other. But it's not over yet.
line.town.tc_day.2: All going to plan so far. Not that there is a plan.
line.town.tc_day_morning.1: Tea first, then we'll see. Too early to plan in the morning.
line.town.tc_day_morning.2: I want to make the market while everything's fresh.
line.town.tc_day_morning.3: Morning's the best time. While everyone sleeps, the town's mine.
line.town.tc_day_morning.4: A whole day's jobs for one morning. I'll start and see how it goes.
line.town.tc_day_evening.1: It was a good day. My feet ache, so it wasn't wasted.
line.town.tc_day_evening.2: I'm worn out by evening. Home now, tea and bed.
line.town.tc_day_kid.1: Three bumps already today and not one tear!
line.town.tc_day_kid.2: We're building a hideout. I won't say where, it's a secret.
line.town.tc_day_kid.3: I'm the captain today. The bench is a ship, don't sit on the stern!
line.town.tc_day_teen.1: Yeah, fine. Lessons, then the club if they let me.
line.town.tc_day_teen.2: Nothing special. Waiting for something to happen.
line.town.tc_day_teen.3: Sitting here thinking what to do. That's a thing to do too.
line.town.tc_day_elder.1: Wake up, get as far as the bench: a good day already.
line.town.tc_day_bench.1: Sitting, watching people. Beats any film.
line.town.tc_day_bench.2: Resting. The bench is warm, the view's good, no hurry at all.
line.town.tc_day_bench.3: Sitting and counting passers-by. You're number forty-three today.
line.town.tc_day_shop.1: Out shopping. The list's at home, I'm working from memory.
line.town.tc_day_shop.2: Choosing. I need one thing and want everything.
line.town.tc_day_eat.1: Eating out today. One has to spoil oneself sometimes.
line.town.tc_day_eat.2: Sitting, waiting for my order. The nicest wait in the world.
line.town.tc_day_walk.1: Out walking. Doctor's orders: ten thousand steps, roughly counted.
line.town.tc_day_walk.2: Walking wherever my eyes lead. They lead towards the sea.
line.town.tc_day_walk.3: Just walking. Thoughts sort themselves onto shelves as you go.
line.town.tc_day_night_walk.1: The day's over and it's too early for bed. So I walk.
line.town.tc_day_night_walk.2: The town's different at night. I don't know it like this by day.
line.town.tc_day_night_walk.3: Can't sleep. The sea murmurs and I feel calmer.
line.town.tc_day_night_walk.4: It's been a long day. I'm walking it off before bed.
line.town.tc_day_fish.1: Fishing. Or rather waiting. Fishing is mostly waiting.
line.town.tc_day_fish.2: Here since first light. The fish are still asleep, I'm not.
line.town.tc_day_fish.3: Biting a little. What matters is the quiet and the flask.
line.town.tc_day_work.1: On my feet all day. I'll breathe out when the shift ends.
line.town.tc_day_work.2: Working. But there's a minute for a decent person.
line.town.tc_day_child.1: Minding the little one. Look away and they're up a tree.
line.town.tc_day_before_work.1: Work soon. I'm catching the last free minutes.
line.town.tc_day_before_work.2: The shift's still ahead. Gathering my strength.
line.town.tc_day_before_work.3: On shift in an hour. Breathing the air in while I can.
line.town.tc_day_before_work.4: Still some time before work. Spending it wisely: doing nothing.
line.town.tc_day_before_school.1: Lessons in a bit. My bag's as heavy as an anchor.
line.town.tc_day_before_school.2: Classes still ahead. I'm finishing my sleep on the move.
line.town.tc_day_before_school.3: A test today. I'm counting on a miracle and my desk-mate.
line.town.tc_day_before_school.4: Off to learn. Knowledge is heavy and I'm the one carrying it.
line.town.tc_day_after_work.1: Done for today. Now the town is mine.
line.town.tc_day_after_work.2: Shift's behind me. I'm walking slowly: I've earned it.
line.town.tc_day_after_work.3: Work's over and the day isn't. I love this hour.
line.town.tc_day_after_work.4: That's it for today. Empty head, and my feet carry me to the sea.
line.town.tc_day_after_school.1: Lessons are over! I'm a free person till supper.
line.town.tc_day_after_school.2: Classes done. I'll do the homework later. Probably.
line.town.tc_day_after_school.3: Freedom! I'll dump my bag at home and out into the yard.
line.town.tc_day_after_school.4: I didn't get asked today. Best day of the week.
line.town.tc_day_off.1: Day off! I'm in no hurry, and it's wonderful.
line.town.tc_day_off.2: Not working today. Learning to do nothing; not very good at it yet.
line.town.tc_day_off.3: A day off. The alarm clock's silent and so is my conscience.
line.town.tc_day_off_school.1: No lessons today! The whole day's mine.
line.town.tc_did_shop.1: Just back from the shop. The bread's still warm, smell that?
line.town.tc_did_shop.2: Shopping's done. Purse lighter, bag heavier.
line.town.tc_did_eat.1: Just up from the table. Now for an hour of going nowhere.
line.town.tc_did_eat.2: Coffee drunk, cake eaten. The day's a success already.
line.town.tc_did_sea.1: Just come from the sea. Lazy waves today, a pleasure to watch.
line.town.tc_did_sea.2: Coming from the shore. The surf's still sounding in my head.
line.town.tc_did_walk.1: One lap of the promenade done. I can sit with a clear conscience.
line.town.tc_did_walk.2: A proper walk, that was. My legs didn't say thanks, my head did.
line.town.tc_did_bench.1: Sat on a bench and talked the whole town over. You too.
line.town.tc_did_bench.2: Coming from the bench. The pigeons are cheekier than ever today.
line.town.tc_did_club.1: Just out of the club. My hands still remember the keys.
line.town.tc_did_club.2: No luck at the club today. I'll win it back tomorrow.
line.town.tc_did_library.1: From the library. Quiet as a submarine in there.
line.town.tc_did_library.2: Half the day over a book. Tired eyes, contented head.
line.town.tc_did_fish.1: Back from fishing. A modest catch, but a bucketful of quiet.
line.town.tc_did_fish.2: The bites were poor. Fish are educated these days.
line.town.tc_did_fair.1: Back from the fun! No money left, but a gingerbread and good spirits.
line.town.tc_did_fair.2: The crowd there! All acquaintances, a word with each one.
line.town.tc_did_culture.1: From the culture house. We clapped till our palms burned.
line.town.tc_did_culture.2: It's good to have somewhere to go of an evening in a town.
line.town.tc_did_sport.1: After training. Everything hurts, even bits I haven't got.
line.town.tc_did_sport.2: A proper workout. Now a pasty is allowed.
line.town.tc_did_garden.1: From the allotment. Soil under the nails is the best manicure.
line.town.tc_did_garden.2: Watered, weeded. The carrots look promising.
line.town.tc_did_play.1: We were playing! Victory was close, then they called us to lunch.
line.town.tc_did_play.2: All run out. Water now, please. A bucket.
line.town.tc_did_school.1: From school. Bag full, head empty.
line.town.tc_did_school.2: Six lessons. Six! I deserve an ice cream.
line.town.tc_did_clinic.1: From the doctor's. I'll live, they say, but less salt.
line.town.tc_did_clinic.2: From my treatments. The queue there is a cure in itself.
line.town.tc_weather.1: Weather's weather. By the sea it's different in an hour anyway.
line.town.tc_weather.2: Can't complain. Though the barometer's up to something.
line.town.tc_weather_rain.1: Pouring and pouring. Still, the allotments are glad.
line.town.tc_weather_rain.2: In rain like this one should sit by a window, not stand here with you.
line.town.tc_weather_rain.3: Rain is just the sea come visiting. We'll bear it.
line.town.tc_weather_snow.1: Snow! The town's cleaner and quieter at once.
line.town.tc_weather_snow.2: Look at it come down. A day's work for the yardmen by morning.
line.town.tc_weather_fog.1: Fog: the lighthouse hoots, the gulls keep quiet. I love it.
line.town.tc_weather_fog.2: Can't see your own nose. Walk carefully.
line.town.tc_weather_cold.2: The frost nips. You should put a scarf on.
line.town.tc_weather_warm.1: What heat! On a day like this all of life is by the water.
line.town.tc_weather_warm.2: So warm. The ice-cream man's the most important person in town today.
line.town.tc_weather_clear.1: A clear sky. On a day like this even a fence is beautiful.
line.town.tc_weather_clear.2: Sunshine! Catch it while you can, we don't get it every day.
line.town.tc_weather_night.1: The stars tonight: you could count them. I get to a hundred and lose track.
line.town.tc_weather_autumn.1: Autumn. Leaves rustle, the sea goes dark. Hat weather soon.
line.town.tc_weather_spring.1: Spring! The starlings are back and the heart is lighter.
line.town.tc_weather_kid.1: I like any weather. Except "come home, it's dark".
line.town.tc_festival.1: A holiday! The whole town's on its feet, even those who usually sit.
line.town.tc_festival.2: Today we celebrate. Chores can wait till tomorrow.
line.town.tc_festival.3: Go to the square, that's where it's all happening.
line.town.tc_festival_kid.1: It's a holiday! I've already got a lollipop cockerel!
line.town.tc_festival_elder.1: I love holidays. At my age each one is a present.
line.town.tc_festival_fair.1: The fair! Walk every stall and take your time. It's a sin to hurry here.
line.town.tc_festival_new_year.1: Happy New Year to come! Have you made your wish yet?
line.town.tc_festival_sea.1: A holiday by the sea! Boats in bunting, the whole shore out celebrating.
line.town.tc_festival_lantern.1: There'll be lanterns this evening. Don't miss it, it's lovely.
line.town.tc_rumour.1: Oh, they talk all right. Good things, don't worry.
line.town.tc_rumour.2: It's a small town. Sneeze at the market and the lighthouse says "bless you".
line.town.tc_rumour_cup.1: They say {1} is yours now. The whole yard is proud.
line.town.tc_rumour_beat.1: They say {1} is still demanding a rematch. The whole club's buzzing.
line.town.tc_rumour_job.1: They say you've got a job {1}. They speak well of you, by the way.
line.town.tc_rumour_tamed.1: They say a bird eats from your hand: {1}. People respect that here.
line.town.tc_rumour_catch.1: They're talking about your catch: {1}! The fishermen envy in silence.
line.town.tc_rumour_tune.1: They say you play "{1}". And cleanly too.
line.town.tc_rumour_kite.1: They talk about your kite. Higher than the lighthouse, they say.
line.town.tc_rumour_garden.1: They say your beds took a prize. Now the allotment folk greet you first.
line.town.tc_rumour_fine.1: They say you were fined on the train. Never mind, it happens.
line.town.tc_rumour_radio.1: The whole house heard your request on the radio. A good choice.
line.town.tc_rumour_crows.1: They say the crows bring you presents. Clever birds, they chose well.
line.town.tc_friend.1: {6} and I go back a long way. Ask {5} about me, you'll hear plenty!
line.town.tc_friend.2: {2}: never a dull moment there. We meet every week.
line.town.tc_friend.3: If you see {5}, say hello from me.
line.town.tc_friend.4: This town would be duller without {3}.
line.town.tc_friend.5: I could go on about {7} for hours. Better meet in person, you won't regret it.
